newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to offer new $1.9 bln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to offer new $1.9 bln bonds.

text.p: The Philippines is offering $1.9 billion new uncollateralised bonds to institutional investors in exchange for the Philippine Brady bonds, finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday.
The government is offering 15-year floating rate bonds and 20-year fixed rate bonds, the interest yields of which would be fixed on September 18.
The Philippine Brady bonds were issued in 1992 as part of the government's debt restructuring programme. The bonds have U.S. Treasury bonds as their collaterals.
"This landmark transaction will distance us further from our history of external debt," De Ocampo told a news conference.
The series A Brady bonds, which have an outstanding $413 million, will mature in year 2018, while the series B, which have an outstanding $1.7 billion, will mature in 2017.
The government will start inviting institutional investors to exchange their Philippine Brady bonds on September 2 until September 20.
The announcement on the acceptance of offers, which will be based on their offered exchange rates, will be on September 23.
The settlement of the exchange will be on October 7.
De Ocampo said the exchange will effectively retire $1.9 billion worth of Brady bonds, and set the benchmark for a 20-year Philippine debt paper in the international debt market.
